text: This story owns no legacy acceptance criterion. The ten criteria AC1 to AC10 of RWB-E2-008 and the ten legacy test cases are owned by RWB-P8-E2008-APP and by RWB-P1-E2008-APP against RWB-P8-E2008-CON, and the seven criteria of this story are new under D-RCV-60. They test only the treatment-side consequence of a match and of a miss, and every identifier, amount, date, count, rule ID and package version they use is copied character for character from the legacy story: case RC-2026-000555, account A-0555, plan T-0701, 12,500.00 THB, 24 installments, 3 paid, due dates 2026-12-15 and 2027-01-15, payment PAY-90001 dated 2026-12-14, package PM-2026.12, rules R-RES-26 and R-RES-27.
why: The Work Package gives this story an empty legacy-criterion list while it is an APP story of a split key, so no legacy scenario can be copied verbatim without claiming a criterion another story owns; the legacy values are still the only allowed ones and the legacy story names each of them.

text: The matched installment and the missed installment reach the plan on the published contract of RWB-P8-E2008-CON: rwb.payment.ProceedsMatched.v1 (EV-25) and rwb.payment.PaymentMissed.v1 (EV-12) on rwb.payment.events.v1 through this service's own consumer group and inbox. The legacy in-process TreatmentApi.recordInstallmentPaid has no operation in any source, so its name, its payload and the element names of the plan position are the contract's own; where the contract freeze chooses a REST write instead of the event, the same treatment write is served by PATCH /treatments/{treatmentId} (API-S2-003) with right U, and no other path is added. The two activity names applyProceedsMatched and holdMissedInstallment, the consumer-group names and the flag rwb.treatment.plan-position are this story's design choice.
why: Three sources describe the route differently (legacy in-process call, Design slide 9 event through the case router, Architecture v5 slide 42 subscription) and no source gives the legacy operation a name, a payload or an inventory entry; the Work Package gives this story RWB-P8-E2008-CON as its only contract dependency, which is the contract that publishes both events.

text: The plan position is derived and not stored: the earliest unpaid due date is computed from first_due_date (DF-TRT-029) and installments_paid (DF-TRT-032) on a monthly cadence, its amount due is installment_amount (DF-TRT-031), and the count of the schedule is installments (DF-TRT-009). The monthly cadence is taken from the legacy plan, whose due dates are 2026-12-15 and 2027-01-15, and from R-RES-25 (SCHEDULE_SET to PLAN_RUNNING) in TSD S2 T4. This story adds no business column; its Flyway version adds only the write key that makes one advance and one miss per due date and the index the read uses.
why: TSD S2 T3.1 has no next due date, no missed due date, no missed amount and no frequency column, and no source says whether the position is stored or computed, while the legacy story fixes the two due dates one month apart and the position must be shown on SCR-14 the same morning.

text: The case status, the plan states and the cure period stay with their owners. The plan states are the RESTRUCTURE states of TSD S2 T4 and are written by the booking story (R-RES-25) and by the broken-plan and shortfall slices (R-RES-27 to R-RES-31); this story moves no plan state and writes no case status, and it reports a stage outcome to the parent CaseWorkflow, which moves the case. The plan side of R-RES-27 is RWB-S2-E2027-APP's and RWB-S2-E3011-APP's, so the criteria of this story name the rule only as the record the miss carries.
why: The legacy story says its story changes no case status and that P3 changes the plan route state, TSD S2 T4 holds the plan states in this service's own machine, the context pack gives rwb-case the case and the workflow, and two sibling stories of the same service already own the breach, the shortfall and the closure.

text: The contract dependency RWB-P8-E2008-CON stands as Draft (realignment v1) and is not approved before this story starts; the story builds against the published contract and its fakes on Day 1, which is the Day-1 rule for an APP story with only a contract dependency. No approval gate is waited on, and the status of the story stays Draft (realignment v1).
why: The run rules of D-RCV-60 require the work to continue without human approval and to record a missing approval as an assumption and continue in Draft status; §R5.7 makes a CON dependency non-blocking and Day 1 for a story whose H list is empty.
